subject: Follow-up: NebulaWorks streaming latency targets & cost levers
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alex Geller <alex.geller@nebulaworks.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: NebulaWorks streaming latency targets & cost levers

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + concrete next steps so we have alignment on SLOs and the levers we can use to hit them.

Recap of requirements you shared
- Streaming/chat use case with average response length ~300 tokens (peak 800).
- P95 latency target: <= 280ms for token-by-token streaming at 512-token context.
- Sustained concurrency target: 1,000 concurrent users at typical activity curve (bursty peaks x2).
- Throughput: ~45 QPS sustained, spikes to ~120 QPS for short windows.
- Retention/ops: customer logs must be retained in-region, and KV cache must respect privacy controls.

Suggested cost/perf levers (first-pass)
1) Continuous batching: short window (10–20ms) to group inflight requests; target 1.5–2x GPU efficiency without visible added latency for streaming starts.
2) Prefix & KV caching: pre-cache first ~64 tokens of frequent prompts; this saves work per request in long-lived chats.
3) Quantization profile: trial q4_k_m for production (balanced perf/cost) and q3/FP16 for quality-sensitive routes.
4) Model variants: offer a smaller low-latency variant for short-turn chats (e.g., 13B quantized) and higher-capacity 70B for complex sessions. Smart routing (latency tier -> cheaper model variant) can cut unit cost ~30%.
5) Fallbacks: plan automatic fallback to regional model shard or lower-precision path when GPUs are saturated.

What we need from you to size the pilot
- A small sample of request traces (timestamps + token counts) to verify burst shape and per-request sizes — I attached a template for a JSON trace.
- Confirmation on strictness of the 280ms P95 (hard SLO vs aspirational).
- Any streaming particulars: do you need immediate token-level streaming start or can we buffer first token for 20ms?

Next steps (proposed)
1) You drop the sample traces into the Drive folder linked below.
2) Ben and I will create a bench plan and run two microbenchmarks: baseline model variant + quantized path (3–4 days).
3) We’ll share a short cost estimate and an SLO attainment plan (bench results + recommended routing).

Attachments: nebula_latency_trace_sample.json (trace template)
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example

Thanks — I’ll coordinate Ben’s benchmark slots once we get the traces.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Geller <alex.geller@nebulaworks.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina.park@nebulaworks.com>, procurement@nebulaworks.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NebulaWorks streaming latency targets & cost levers

Priyom — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications:
- 280ms P95 is our target for interactive chats. If that’s a hard SLO we may be open to a 99th percentile window for very short spikes, but we want 95th consistently.
- We need token-at-a-time streaming to our UI (cannot buffer the first token >25ms).
- The burst shape is typically 08:30–09:15 and 18:00–19:00 PST; spikes can be 2–3x sustained levels for ~5–7 minutes.

I’ve uploaded a small trace set and a CSV with token length distribution to the shared Drive. Lina (cc'ed) will own procurement/contracting — she’ll need a clear pilot scope and an estimate of monthly committed spend for Dedicated vs Hosted pilot.

Appreciate you taking this on — we can sync early next week after your bench?

— Alex
Alex Geller
Head of Product, NebulaWorks
alex.geller@nebulaworks.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Alex Geller <alex.geller@nebulaworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 18:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: NebulaWorks streaming latency targets & cost levers

Thanks — digging into the requirements. A few quick technical notes from the bench plan perspective:

- Batching window: we should start at 10ms and experiment up to 25ms. For token-at-a-time streaming the headroom is tight; aim for 10–12ms to avoid first-token delay.
- KV cache: recommend two-tier cache: 1) prefix cache (64-token) in warm GPU cache; 2) optional external Redis for session checkpoints. The first saves ~12–18% work on repeated prompts.
- Quant profiles: schedule runs for q4_k_m and q3_k; q4 should be baseline for cost-focused routes.
- Model plumbing: run a split test: 13B q4 vs 70B q4_k_m for a 48-hour window under representative load to observe P95 delta and tail behavior.

I attached the benchmark plan spreadsheet with test matrices and time estimates. I can run the initial microbench tomorrow morning if you confirm available traces & API keys.

Attachments: redwood-benchmark-plan.xlsx

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

- Expected per-token unit costs for the production configuration (with the recommended quant profile).
- Any minimum commitment or setup fee.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: NebulaWorks streaming latency targets & cost levers

Lina — thanks. I’ve drafted a short cost summary (attached PDF) and a high-level pilot scope below so finance can evaluate quickly. Ben and I will run the bench today and I’ll follow up with measured P95 numbers and an updated estimate by EOD Monday.

Pilot (recommended) — 6 weeks- Config: Hosted pilot on dedicated GPU pool; primary path uses 70B q4_k_m with fallback to 13B q4 for <2s chats. Continuous batching 10ms window; prefix cache enabled for top 15% prompts.- Sizing: baseline estimate to meet 1,000 concurrent target with 2x burst headroom: 6 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (provisioned as a Dedicated pilot).- Estimated monthly cost (pilot pro-rated): Dedicated pilot ~ $62,000/month; Hosted burst-enabled pilot ~ $48,000/month.- Per-token estimates (approx): 70B q4_k_m generation: $0.00095 per token; 13B q4 generation: $0.00032 per token. These are preliminary pending bench results.

Contract and discounts: Marissa is cc'd. We can provide a pilot discount for a 3-month commit (10–15% depending on licensing and data controls).

Attachments: cost-estimate-summary.pdf
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/98765

If that aligns, Lina — can you confirm the procurement cadence (review by next Tue?) and any PO/contract templates we should use?

— Priyom
